The ancient-woodland-status collector last ran on 8 July 2026.
Sites of special scientific interest are nationally protected sites.
SSSIs can be designated for wildlife or geological features.
SSSIs are designated by Natural England.
The SSSI dataset reports one provider.
The SSSI collector last ran on 27 July 2026.
The SSSI dataset is licensed under Open Government Licence version 3.0.
The Planning Data API supports latitude and longitude queries for entities intersecting a point.
A single Planning Data query can request multiple datasets.
The Planning Data API can query heritage and environmental designations using a UPRN.
The documented environmental query includes SSSI, ancient woodland and flood-risk-zone datasets.
The time-stamped DSM product is an archive of raster elevation data produced by the Environment Agency.
Site-specific LiDAR surveys have been carried out across England since 1998.
Some locations such as coastal areas have been surveyed multiple times.
Time-stamped DSM data is available at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m resolutions.
The DSM is produced from the last-return LiDAR signal.
DSM values include vehicles, buildings, vegetation and the terrain surface.
Time-stamped DSM data is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters.
The GeoTIFF rasters are supplied in 5 km ZIP packages.
The elevation values are presented in metres.
The elevation values are referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The raster data is aligned to the Ordnance Survey National Grid.
The time-stamped DSM dataset states a vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
The Environment Agency replaced ASCII delivery of composite elevation products with GeoTIFF.
GeoTIFF was selected as an open-standard GIS format.
GeoTIFF was selected for efficient elevation-data storage.
The Environment Agency states that GeoTIFF data volumes are on average five times smaller than the former ASCII data.
Smaller GeoTIFF files enable faster internet downloads.
GeoTIFF enables delivery through image services and WCS services.
GeoTIFF aligns composite elevation delivery with National LiDAR Programme products.
The LiDAR specification requires absolute height RMSE below plus or minus 15 cm.
Expected relative height error is no more than plus or minus 5 cm.
Absolute RMSE compares LiDAR elevations with a ground-truth survey.
A 1 m DSM survey requires at least one point per square metre on average.
